Recently i've been getting some cycling done despite being quite sore most of the time. Each morning with my morning round of painkillers, i'll also have a protein shake and some thermobol caffeine free, and once the painkillers start to kick in i chuck myself out the door on the bike and set off. The caffeine and protein make my mind and body feel almost like a normal human, and the painkillers keep the worst of it away so I can actually get a good bike ride in before coming back and resting the rest of the day.

The endorphins and dopamine from the exercise also help make me feel better and dull the pain too, so not only am I able to get some exercise done, it helps with the pancreatitis pain too! :) I'd definitely recommend a good protein powder to everyone struggling with lack of energy. A couple of my friends have already been giving it a shot and are reporting that it's really helped them. It just gives you a decent energy boost but not in a hyper sugar rush sort of way, or an up and down yo-yo effect either. It just lets you feel active without being hyper, and gives your body fuel, rather than just caffeine making your brain feel like it's working too fast.

If i really want to try and do something I take a mix of green tea tablets and protein shake, and it gives both body and mind boost which most mornings is a definite bonus :P I'm not a morning person at all normally.

As far as protein shakes go, the higher the protien % the better. I'm not interested in "gains" from carbs which many of the "protein" shakes contain, so you need to be careful when reading which one to buy. I got one similar to this http://www.argos.co.uk/static/Product/partNumber/9292747.htm as my latest round, although the actual one i got was USN Whey Protein Premium - Strawberry Cream, which actually tastes really nice. I also got Primal26 as Men's Health gave it protein powder of the year award or something, and it's good but tastes nastier than the USN one. I don't notice a huge difference between the effects them, so I'd probably go with the USN one in the future, on taste alone.

Feel free to message me if you want any info on the green tea tablets or protein shakes i use, as i've experimented a bit with different ones whilst i was at uni and used to exercise a lot more before my pancreatitis got worse. It's such a relief to have SOMETHING that gives me a bit of energy to function when I need to though :)
